title: GroundTruth
description: The seeded defects in one fixture app, plus what a correct finding about each would have to say. Read only by the scoring harness — never exposed to the agent under evaluation (design-doc §14).

fixture_id.description: Directory name of the fixture, e.g. 'bug-001-implementation-bug'.

description.description: What the app is supposed to do. Safe to show a human reading results; not given to the agent.

defects.description: Seeded defects. Usually exactly one per fixture, so that a miss is unambiguous.

site.description: Where the defect actually is. The scorer matches a finding to this defect by path, then by symbol.

expected.description: What a correct finding must say. Each axis is scored independently, mirroring the finding schema's separation of axes (design-doc §11).

classification_type.description: Acceptable values. A list rather than a single value because the taxonomy has genuine overlap (e.g. an over-specified assertion is arguably both flaky_test and test_defect) — design-doc §17.

classification_type_preferred.description: The single best answer, when the acceptable list has more than one. Reported separately so taxonomy ambiguity is measured rather than hidden.

concerns.description: Concerns the finding must include. Extra concerns beyond these are not penalised; missing ones are.

root_cause_status.description: Acceptable root_cause.status values. For a flaky-test fixture this deliberately excludes 'confirmed' — confirming an application defect there is a wrong answer, not a strong one.

min_severity.description: Least severe acceptable rating. P0 is most severe, so 'P2' accepts P0/P1/P2.

root_cause_keywords.description: Groups of synonyms. A group is satisfied if ANY of its strings appears (case-insensitive) in the finding's root_cause.explanation; root cause counts as correct only if ALL groups are satisfied. Grouping avoids demanding exact phrasing while still requiring the right mechanism.

notes.description: Why this defect is non-trivial to find — e.g. which existing tests pass despite it.

false_positive_controls.description: Paths/symbols in this fixture that are deliberately correct. A finding anchored here is counted a false positive, which is how §14's 'avoid false positives on the other fixtures' becomes measurable.
